plan.angle: Title if the paper has a tirzepatide-specific result: 'Tirzepatide: Does Losing More Weight Mean Losing More Muscle?' Otherwise: 'GLP-1 Weight Loss: Does Losing More Mean Losing More Muscle?' Then say 'in people on obesity medicines, including tirzepatide'. Open with the paper's verified finding, labelled 'observational, muscle estimated by a device, not a trial', and name the exact drugs and population the paper covered. Add one SURMOUNT-1 anchor ('in a body-scan substudy, about a quarter of the weight lost was lean mass, which isn't all muscle') that matches L1 word for word. Then two recommended habits: strength training started gently, and protein at each meal unless your clinician limits it. One GI line. 'Not personal advice' plus the prescriber line. Last line: 'Full breakdown on our channel, link in the description.'

package.title: Tirzepatide Weight Loss: Are You Losing Muscle Too? #shorts
package.description:
Observational study (59 adults, mostly on tirzepatide, ~7 months): losing more weight was linked to losing more device-estimated muscle. Strength training and protein may help, if your clinician says it's safe (protein may be limited, say, for kidney disease). Common side effects include nausea, diarrhea and constipation.
Source: J Clin Med 2026;15(20):8008
#Tirzepatide #GLP1 #MuscleHealth #WeightLoss #StrengthTraining
Not personal advice. Talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you.

social.facebook_caption:
Losing weight on a GLP-1 and worried it might be coming from muscle, not just fat? That's a fair question to ask.

A new observational study (Oct 2026, 59 adults, mostly on tirzepatide, ~7 months) found the typical person lost 9.9 kg of fat and 2.3 kg of device-estimated muscle — and losing more weight overall was linked to losing more estimated muscle. In tirzepatide's SURMOUNT-1 trial (adults with obesity or overweight, no diabetes, 72 weeks), a body-scan substudy found about a quarter of weight lost was lean mass, which isn't all muscle.

Two habits that may help: gentle strength training at least twice a week if your clinician says it's safe, and protein at each meal unless your clinician limits it (say, for kidney disease). Common side effects like nausea, diarrhea or constipation can make big protein portions tough, so smaller protein portions may help.

Save this for your next workout, or share it with someone on a GLP-1.

Not personal advice. Talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you.

#Tirzepatide #GLP1 #MuscleHealth

factcheck.summary: The claims hold up against the sources. src1 is a real paper: J Clin Med 2026;15(20):8008, published 15 October 2026. It's a retrospective observational cohort of 59 adults (53 on tirzepatide, 6 on semaglutide), measured with InBody 770 over a median of 7.0 months. Median losses were 9.9 kg of fat and 2.3 kg of device-estimated muscle. Each extra 5 percentage points of weight loss was linked to 2.47 percentage points more relative estimated muscle loss. So s2 and s4 are accurate, and both are labelled observational. In the SURMOUNT-1 body-scan substudy (n=160: 124 tirzepatide, 36 placebo), 26% of the weight lost was lean mass with tirzepatide versus 25% with placebo, so "about a quarter, similar to placebo" in s3 is correct. The WHO 2020 guideline supports strength training on 2 or more days a week. The nutrition advisory supports eating protein at meals and smaller meals to help with stomach side effects. The kidney caveat, the clinician-safety caveat, "Not personal advice", the prescriber line and the playbook funnel call to action are all there. I found four small fixes: a source-label mismatch, a source tag on the 2-day figure, one on-screen card that misses the muted-viewer test, and a small narration tweak in s4.

issues.claim: Nutritional priorities advisory listed as American Journal of Clinical Nutrition with URL PMC12304835
issues.problem: The advisory came out in several journals at the same time (AJCN, Obesity and others). The PMC12304835 page is the Obesity (Silver Spring) version: 2025 Aug;33(8):1475–1503. So the publisher label doesn't match the linked page.
issues.fix: Change the publisher to "Obesity (Silver Spring), joint advisory from ACLM, ASN, OMA and TOS", year 2025, and keep the URL https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12304835/

issues.claim: Guidelines say at least two days a week (src4, src5)
issues.problem: The '2 days' figure comes from WHO (src4). The GLP-1 advisory (src5) says strength training at least three times a week, so tagging src5 to the 2-day line misattributes the figure.
issues.fix: Set s5 source_ids to ["src4"] for the 2-day figure. Alternatively keep both and change the narration to: "Habit one: strength training, started gently. WHO guidelines say at least two days a week, if your clinician says it's safe."

issues.claim: on_screen_text "The catch" with narration "losing more was linked to losing more estimated muscle"
issues.problem: Muted-viewer test: the card shows only "The catch", so the finding and its observational label never appear on screen. The narration also leaves out what "losing more" refers to.
issues.fix: Narration: "The catch: in the new study, losing more weight was linked to losing more estimated muscle." On-screen text: "More weight lost, more estimated muscle lost (observational)"

issues.problem: The label is too long to read on a Short stat pill and repeats the narration. This is a readability issue only.
issues.fix: stat_label: "Tirzepatide, SURMOUNT-1 body-scan substudy (n=160), 72 wks: lean share of weight lost, similar to placebo"

audio.soundNotes: Music sits at -13.5 dB under voice and -13.4 in pauses, both at the edge of target, so pulled the whole bed down about 0.6 dB (gain 0.93) to land it centered in the -12/-15 window with pauses nearer -14. Found and fixed two real masking risks during speech (cue 54 pop at -7.2 dB, cues 69/70 blips at -9.6/-10.3 dB) by cutting them hard into the -14/-20 speech range. Thinned five SFX swarms that exceeded the 3-4-per-second rule (around the "1 in 4" stat at 31.2s, "lean mass ≠ all muscle" at 33.2s, "protein at each meal" at 51.4s, "smaller portions" at 62.3s, and the outro at 70.6s) by dropping redundant ticks/pops/blips and keeping one clear whoosh/ding/pop per beat. Left two already-inaudible swell cues (30, 51/52, around -35/-42 dB rel) alone since they're not masking anything and a fix would need an unrealistic gain jump. Added five bespoke accents for key story beats: a data-reveal chime on the 9.9-vs-2.3kg stat, a soft heartbeat pulse under "about 1 in 4," a tension string pluck on "the catch," an energetic snap on the strength-training tip, and a calm reassuring piano note under "not personal advice" — all kept at felt, under-dialogue levels.
